Yes, you caught something that my editors and I missed. Oops.
Best,
Richard

comments.author: P. Ban
comments.html:
Has anyone written a novel about the introduction of nanobots into fairly contemporary American society? You mentioned in K. Nexus Assimilation that Jamal missed a wine buzz and that drug use was negatively affected. I was wondering (before I began reading your works) about such an introduction and how various folk would react. Would the introduction be covert (via water supplies or slipped into breweries) or overt (how would those who chose drugs over nanobots be regarded or treated by society)? Your earlier works suggested a whole host of problems created, but Africa seemed to be the focus of those speculations, not America.
Dialysis used to permit a cycle of use/abuse followed by “cure” created a whole new set of reflections upon possible changes in society.
Any suggestions for a serious novel I’ve not encountered? If you have already written one, I am going to be very embarrassed.

replies.author: Richard Phillips
replies.html: Thank you. I’m sure someone else must have written on this topic but I haven’t read any such novels.

comments.author: Amy
comments.html: Will you be revisiting all these characters in a different series perhaps or are you finished with them altogether?

I do plan on doing a follow-on to the Rho Agenda series picking up on some of the characters once I complete my epic fantasy series, The Endarian Prophecy.
Best,
Richard
